summary: This sermon examines Jonah chapter 2, arguing that the book is not about a whale but about self-righteousness—how we think we deserve God's grace while deeming others unworthy. The preacher draws parallels to modern social media algorithms that reinforce tribal thinking and confronts both the self-righteous religious person and the wayward sinner with God's patient, compassionate grace.
key_points: Self-righteousness distorts reality, leading us to condemn others, accuse God, and justify ourselves
Jonah did not pray until after God saved him, then used religious language to justify himself without true repentance
Salvation belongs to the Lord alone and is freely given to all who humbly repent
God is patient with both the self-righteous prophet and the wicked Ninevites
The parable of the prodigal son mirrors Jonah's story—both older and younger brothers need the Father's grace
big_idea: Salvation belongs to God alone, who extends compassionate grace both to the self-righteous religious and to those deemed unworthy, calling all to humble repentance rather than self-justification.
title: JONAH: Self-Righteousness & Salvation
